title: Argumentation Belongs in Every Classroom
author: Stefan Bauschard
summary: Stefan Bauschard argues that argumentation belongs in every classroom and uses two timely robot controversies — the FCC's move to ban Chinese-made robots and a $57,590 classroom robot paused after community pushback — as curriculum material. The article introduces the Toulmin model of argument structure: claim, grounds, and warrant, with the warrant being the most commonly skipped and most important element. The author provides two complete 45-page classroom kits that teach argumentation through these live controversies. The kits are parallel in structure across different controversies so students can watch the method transfer. The core thesis is that instructional redesign — particularly around argumentation — should precede AI integration, because good argumentation instruction gives students the framework to evaluate any claim, including claims about AI itself.
points: Instructional redesign, especially in argumentation, should precede AI integration — schools that acquire AI first and ask questions second have the sequence backwards.
Live, unresolved controversies make better argumentation material than textbook cases, because they force students to build cases rather than look up answers.
The Toulmin model's warrant — the reasoning licensing the leap from evidence to claim — is the most skipped and most important part of any argument.
Two parallel 45-page classroom kits on robot controversies teach argumentation structure that transfers to any subject or controversy.
The rubric grades argumentation structure, never the position taken — students can argue either side without affecting their grade.
quotes: Instructional redesign should come before AI integration. Schools keep acquiring the technology first and asking what to do with it second.

Nothing teaches argumentation like a fight nobody has settled yet — the textbook controversy has an answer waiting in the back of the book, but a live one forces students to do what adults are doing right now.
The warrant is the part almost everyone skips, and it is where arguments are actually won and lost.
Say the warrant out loud and suddenly there is something to debate.
The argumentation structure is the constant; the controversy is a plug-in.
